claim_scope: January 2025 order paused refugee-program entry and decisions pending review, with stated exceptions and recurring reports.

source_checks.supports: Order dated January 20, 2025; suspends USRAP entry beginning January 27, pauses refugee application decisions, permits joint case-by-case national-interest exceptions, and directs an initial review and recurring 90-day reports.
source_checks.limits: Does not establish later review or litigation outcomes, permanent program termination, asylum/TPS/T/U visa changes, or agency consolidation.

finding: The mapped official order directly supports the narrowed proposal. Its long description correctly distinguishes a temporary suspension/review from termination of other protections.
action: Retain the narrowed wording and official source.

claim_scope: Project 2025 proposals for DOJ intervention in some local prosecution decisions and court requests to end consent decrees.

source_checks.supports: Brennan Center analysis describes proposed DOJ action against local prosecutors over policies labeled rule-of-law deficiencies, including some non-prosecution decisions, and proposed ending DOJ consent decrees through requests to courts.
source_checks.limits: This is analysis of proposals and projected effects, not evidence the measures were implemented; DOJ cannot unilaterally terminate court decrees.

finding: The proposed copy attributes the policies to the Brennan Center/Project 2025 and disclaims implementation. It excludes the frozen entry's unsupported claims about opposition arrests, protest bans, citizenship revocation, and organization dissolution.

claim_scope: Interior/BLM's 2018 revision of the 2016 Waste Prevention Rule.

source_checks.supports: DOI announced September 18, 2018 that BLM finalized a rule revising the 2016 Waste Prevention/Venting and Flaring Rule; it describes the agency's stated rationale.
source_checks.limits: Press release reflects the department's framing and says Federal Register publication was forthcoming at release time.

source_checks.access: HTTP 200; Federal Register PDF text read
source_checks.supports: Final rule revises/rescinds specified 2016 requirements and gives November 27, 2018 effective date.
source_checks.limits: The formal rule is the source for operative provisions and effective date.

source_checks.access: URL appears in proposal.source_urls; unrelated to the BLM rule
source_checks.supports: Nothing about the rule.
source_checks.limits: Contradicts the proposal's official DOI/GovInfo source mapping and must be removed.

finding: The factual mapping is supported by official sources, but the proposal's own source_urls field contains only an unrelated Facebook Wikipedia page. Align the source list with the DOI and Federal Register URLs before accepting the proposal.
action: Replace the unrelated source_urls entry with the mapped DOI and GovInfo URLs; keep the claims within those official records.

claim_scope: Trump's March 13, 2018 announcement of Tillerson's departure and Pompeo's nomination.

source_checks.access: Direct request and Firecrawl resolved to CNBC's 404/not-found page
source_checks.supports: The exact cited page is unavailable and provides no article text for the mapped personnel-action facts.
source_checks.limits: No substitute URL was counted as evidence; the factual account may be plausible but is not verified by this exact citation.

finding: The single exact citation cannot be read and there is no event-specific accessible source in the proposal mapping. Motive claims are correctly excluded, but the corrected personnel-action claim still lacks verified URL-to-fact support.
action: Hold until a readable exact contemporaneous or primary source is cited and checked.

claim_scope: Arpaio's criminal-contempt finding and Trump's pre-sentencing pardon in August 2017.

source_checks.supports: Lists Trump's pardon of Joe Arpaio for contempt of court before sentencing and no sentence imposed.
source_checks.limits: Clemency list establishes pardon and recorded offense, not motive.

source_checks.supports: Documents the criminal-contempt proceedings/finding and procedural posture.
source_checks.limits: Court record supports the finding, not a quid pro quo.

source_checks.supports: Explains pardon-related posture; there was no final judgment of conviction before pardon and the proceeding was dismissed with prejudice.
source_checks.limits: Do not imply the pardon erased historical court findings or establish corrupt exchange.

finding: The title and copy distinguish a contempt finding from a final judgment and avoid claiming a corrupt bargain. The primary court and DOJ records support the narrowed account.

claim_scope: AP's tracker of selected 2024 campaign promises and its outcome labels/method fields.

source_checks.access: AP live tracker retrieved via Firecrawl; page metadata/content dated updated December 3, 2025
source_checks.supports: AP describes a tracker for selected promises and uses labels including Kept, In progress, and It's complicated.
source_checks.limits: It is a changing tracker; observations need an as-of date and do not show effects on Trump's messaging.

source_checks.access: HTTP 429; archived snapshot not readable in this review
source_checks.supports: No snapshot-specific facts independently verified.
source_checks.limits: The proposed long copy relies on this URL for archive contents, date, labels, and action methods; the source list proposed for the revised record omits the archive even though citation_url_dispositions says it was used.

finding: The live AP source can support a narrow description of the tracker and current labels. The archived snapshot, specific methods, and dated-view claims cannot be verified from the exact archive URL; the copy also conflicts about whether that archive remains a retained source.
action: Use only facts visible on the live AP page with an explicit retrieval/as-of date, or provide an accessible archive URL and align source_urls; retain no claim about messaging impact or March 4 totals.

claim_scope: AP's report that at least 16 Epstein-related files disappeared from DOJ's public webpage less than a day after posting.

source_checks.access: AP article retrieved via Firecrawl at its canonical article URL
source_checks.supports: Reports at least 16 files were no longer available on DOJ's public webpage less than a day after posting, identifies the reported photo among the files, and says DOJ would continue reviewing/redacting materials.
source_checks.limits: Does not establish destruction of source records, permanence, motive, or political narrative-control intent.

finding: The proposal accurately attributes the count and timing to AP and distinguishes website availability from destruction or motive.

claim_scope: FTC-requested 1988 civil enforcement case concerning Holiday/Bally stock acquisitions and $750,000 penalty settlement.

source_checks.supports: FTC says it asked DOJ to file a civil complaint and reports Trump's agreement to a $750,000 civil penalty settlement.
source_checks.limits: The release describes civil antitrust/premerger-notification enforcement, not a criminal prosecution; settlement is not an admission of violation.

source_checks.supports: Identifies the civil case and links the complaint/final judgment.
source_checks.limits: Does not support the frozen Foreign Policy category or criminal guilt.

finding: The corrected title and descriptions accurately call this a civil case and penalty, and the official FTC materials support the reported transaction context and disposition.
action: Retain the civil-action framing and official FTC sources.

claim_scope: Frozen record alleges a 2007 Moscow contract and hundreds of millions in Russian-project earnings.

source_checks.supports: Reports Sergei Millian's account of drafts for a separate Moscow real-estate project around a later Trump visit; he said drafts were shared with Russian businesspeople but did not go further. It separately describes Russian buyers of Trump properties in the United States.
source_checks.limits: Does not support a 2007 executed contract or hundreds of millions earned from a Russian project; the US-property figure is a different claim.

finding: The proposal itself says identity/date must be resolved and changes no fields. The accessible article concerns a separate draft-stage project, so using that copy to replace the frozen 2007 event would silently change event identity.
action: Keep this frozen event excluded/on hold pending event-identity evidence; do not substitute the later draft-project account.

claim_scope: CDC's posting and removal of a COVID airborne-transmission guidance draft in September 2020 and its stated explanation.

source_checks.supports: Reports revised guidance displayed September 18 and removed September 21; CDC said a draft had been posted before technical review and recommendations were being updated.
source_checks.limits: Does not identify who posted/removed it or establish outside political influence in this specific episode.

source_checks.access: HTTP 202 response with no readable article text
source_checks.supports: No additional facts independently verified from this exact URL.
source_checks.limits: Do not rely on this inaccessible duplicate for technical details; CNN covers the narrow posting/removal and agency explanation.

finding: CNN directly supports the proposed dated web-page change and CDC's reported explanation. The proposal appropriately separates earlier political-interference allegations and does not assign responsibility for this page.
action: Retain the narrow claims on CNN support; either remove the unreadable Seattle Times URL or re-verify it before relying on it.

claim_scope: Redwood's ACIP presentation on thimerosal on June 26, 2025, and separately reported CDC vaccine-safety hiring.

source_checks.supports: Reports that Lyn Redwood presented on thimerosal at the June 26 ACIP meeting and identifies her Children’s Health Defense role.
source_checks.limits: The proposal maps this URL to presentation/date facts; keep claims tied to those reported facts.

source_checks.supports: Attributes to CDC officials the report that Redwood was being hired for vaccine-safety work; says she was scheduled to present about thimerosal.
source_checks.limits: Hiring is source-attributed reporting; the article's pre-meeting schedule alone does not prove a presentation occurred.

finding: The mapped sources support the core event and attributed hiring report. The staged long description additionally attributes study-citation and CDC-scientist-response details to CNN, but no CNN URL is present in proposal.source_urls or the source-to-fact map; those details need a citation or removal. Avoid presenting the CBS-reported hire as a confirmed formal appointment/title.
action: Narrow the long copy to the mapped NBC/CBS facts, or add and map the exact CNN article for its additional claims.

claim_scope: DOJ's $1.776 billion Anti-Weaponization Fund, commission, IRS-settlement context, and reported legal challenge.

source_checks.supports: Announces the $1.776 billion fund, claims process, and five-member commission structure.
source_checks.limits: States the administration's own description and process; not an adjudicated finding of targeting.

source_checks.supports: Reports the Trump/IRS tax-record lawsuit settlement context and fund creation.
source_checks.limits: Use for reported context, not as a judicial endorsement of the fund.

source_checks.supports: Reports a further lawsuit in which plaintiffs asked a judge to block distribution of money and challenged the fund's legality.
source_checks.limits: The article does not explicitly say that no payments had been made by May 22; a request to block distribution is not proof of zero prior payments.

finding: The fund, settlement context, commission, and legal challenge are supported. The mapped assertion that CNN reported no payouts by May 22 is not in the accessible article text; the staged short/medium/long repeat it and need that assertion removed or supported separately.
action: Retain the fund/settlement/commission and lawsuit facts; delete the no-payout assertion unless a direct source establishes it as of May 22.

claim_scope: NYT-reported SEC treatment of crypto enforcement matters during Trump's second term, as summarized by Cointelegraph.

source_checks.supports: Attributes to a December 14, 2025 NYT report that since Trump took office the SEC paused, dropped investigations related to, or dismissed about 60% of cases involving crypto companies/projects.
source_checks.limits: The source says about 60%, describes multiple outcomes, and does not show all matters were dropped or that political ties caused decisions.

source_checks.access: Direct request returned HTTP 403; NYT body not read
source_checks.supports: No direct fact independently verified from this exact NYT URL.
source_checks.limits: Cointelegraph's article links a different NYT path (`/times-sec-cryptocurrency-analysis.html`); the proposal's NYT URL does not match that linked path.

finding: The proposed title/copy say more than 60% and define a denominator of matters active when the term began, which the accessible Cointelegraph summary does not establish. The accessible source supports only about 60% since taking office and includes paused, related investigations dropped, or dismissed. Keep NYT attribution and no causal favoritism claim.
action: Revise the percentage, time frame, and outcome wording to match Cointelegraph exactly; correct or drop the inaccessible/mismatched NYT URL.

claim_scope: The late-night January 24, 2025 dismissals of about 17 inspectors general, effective immediately.

source_checks.supports: Reports the late-Friday/January 24 dismissals, immediate effect, and an approximate count of roughly 17 watchdogs.
source_checks.limits: Count is approximate and the described event is the January 2025 inspector-general action; it does not establish a separate June FBI personnel episode or a legal conclusion that the dismissals were unlawful.

source_checks.access: NYT page not independently readable in this review
source_checks.supports: No additional facts independently verified from this URL; AP supports the narrowed account.
source_checks.limits: Do not rely on inaccessible NYT text for details absent from AP.

finding: The proposed title and account use an approximate count, date, and immediate-effect description consistent with AP, while excluding unsupported June claims and not declaring the firings unlawful.

source_checks.supports: Nothing about entry-6199's event.
